generated.title: San Francisco 1906: The Earthquake That Devastated a City
generated.description:
On April 18, 1906, just after five in the morning, a magnitude 7.9 earthquake struck on the San Andreas Fault.

There, the Pacific and North American plates slide past each other, sideways. The fault broke along nearly three hundred miles of Northern California, and near Point Reyes the ground was offset by about twenty feet. Broken water mains left firefighters struggling as fires burned for days. Early official reports underestimated the death toll, now believed to number in the thousands.

Scientists mapped the broken ground, and Harry Reid explained what they saw: rock bends, stores energy, then snaps back. We still call it elastic rebound.
